nodes.title: VIS: list the papers the picked authors or topics light
nodes.body:
Picking an author or topic lights their papers on the map, but you couldn't see them as a list or jump to one. Now a list of them appears under the picks, the way search lists its results:

- one row per paper, in program order: the title, then the day, time and session;
- a dot in each pick's colour, so a paper two picks share gets both;
- a click pins the paper's first lit square and moves the map to it.

This holds for authors, keywords, cited people and cited works, which share the code. Of the three mockups, this was the one-list design.

**How:**
- The row is search's own, split out as `resultRow` (`packages/search/src/resultsList.ts`), so the two lists build rows the same way. The box style moved from `#search-results` to a shared `.results-list` class; search's box keeps its id and its panel sizing.
- An overlay's controls now get the same `travelTo(id)` its focus panel already had (`renderControls`, `packages/shell/src/overlays/types.ts`). The tests that call `renderControls` pass a do-nothing `travelTo`.
- The list reads the same names for each square that the map lights by (`namesAt` now takes a square id), so the list and the map can't disagree. That matters for the citation overlays, which light only the squares holding a work.

**Desktop** (two authors picked; the panel scrolls the list):
![vis-authors-panel--desktop](https://github.com/danyelf/torahmap/blob/4a4909c9cb3f5d6a0f5fcea5edd358aabf92a91e/vis-authors-panel--desktop.png?raw=true)

**Phone** (the list is below the picks, in the sheet):
![vis-authors-panel--phone](https://github.com/danyelf/torahmap/blob/4a4909c9cb3f5d6a0f5fcea5edd358aabf92a91e/vis-authors-panel--phone.png?raw=true)

**To look:** on the preview, open the VIS map with `?overlay=authors&authors=Jeffrey Heer,Hyeok Kim`, click a paper in the list, and try Cited works the same way. This branch starts from main, so until #576 is merged a paper with no text still lights only its abstract square.

Closes #577

- **In the citation overlays, a click went to the paper's first square, which is usually unlit there:** fixed in `d34d9464`. A click now goes to the first lit square, with a test.
- **The list read per-paper names while the map reads per-square names, agreeing only because of today's data:** fixed in `d34d9464`. The list is built from the squares the map lights.
- **On a phone the list scrolled inside the panel's own scroll:** fixed in `d34d9464`. The list has no height limit, so the panel scrolls it.
- **"N papers" was written in two places:** fixed in `d34d9464`; it's one helper now.

- **Typing keeps the find box's focus; moving the style to a class changes nothing for search; `travelTo` beside search's own click handler is not a real duplication:** checked, no change.

nodes.title: One rule for the popup when the pin changes (createApp restructure, hover and pin)
nodes.body:
Refs #558. Stacked on #573; merge that first, and this PR's base becomes main.

**The problem.** Four places change the pinned verse: a reader's pin, a reader's unpin, a story stop, and a link or Back. Each fixed up the popup its own way. `pinItem` drew the pin, `unpinItem` hid the popup, a story stop hid it only if the stop dropped a pin, and a link hid it whenever the link named no verse. A fresh audit of hover, pin and focus (the next option in #558) found those differences accidental, not deliberate.

**What the audit concluded.** One function owning hover, pin and focus together isn't worth it. What follows a pin depends on who asked (taking the map from the story, telemetry, the URL, centring the camera), not just on what changed. A single `setFocus` would end up needing three kinds of caller and ordering rules, which moves the logic rather than removing it. The useful step turned out smaller still: one rule for the popup.

**The change** (`packages/shell/src/main.ts`):
- `showPin()` draws the popup once the pin changes: the pinned verse, else the hovered verse as a hover, else nothing. `pinItem`, `unpinItem`, the story stop and the link restore call it instead of their own fix-ups.
- `refreshPopup` is unchanged. It redraws what the popup shows and never hides it, because a hovered verse's popup stays up after the mouse leaves the map, so its words can be clicked.
- The story frame's write of the verse under a still mouse becomes `followPointer()`.

**The one visible difference.** With a mouse, unpinning a verse while the pointer rests on it (by Escape, or by clicking the pinned verse) now leaves that verse in the popup as an ordinary hover. Before, the popup disappeared until the mouse moved. The same holds after a story stop that drops its pin, or a link with no verse, while the mouse is over the map. Touch is unaffected: a touch never sets a hover.

**Left alone, for Danyel to decide:**
- While a story scrolls under a still mouse, the popup and the overlay's focus don't follow the verse now under the pointer (they do follow a moving mouse).
- The arrow-key step doesn't stop a camera glide still running from a search result click, so the glide could carry the camera off the stepped-to verse. That's from reading the code; untried.

**Checks.**
- Unit tests: 3,206 passed.
- Two new layout tests:
  - "unpinning a verse under the pointer leaves it in the popup, as a hover" fails on main, where the popup hides.
  - "a word searched from a hovered verse's popup leaves the popup up" guards the case the first version broke.
- Layout suite: 513 passed. Loading suite: 51 passed, run by hand.

**To look at on the preview:** pin a verse, leave the mouse on it, press Escape. The popup should stay up, unpinned. Then hover a verse, move onto its popup, and click a word to search it: the popup should stay.

nodes.title: Rebuild a tool panel on a link or a stop only when its tool changed
nodes.body:
Closes #569

**The problem.** Opening a link, pressing Back, or reaching a story stop cleared both tool panels and built them again from scratch, even when the link named the same tools, for example when Back only pinned a verse again. A rebuild loses the panel's focus and scroll position, and sends the search's `replaced` telemetry, so that event counted redraws rather than a search being replaced.

**The change.**
- `toolsChange` (`packages/shell/src/tools.ts`) also says, for each tool, whether what a link names of it changed (`linked`), comparing the parameters each state would write.
- `setTools` (`packages/shell/src/main.ts`) still takes the tools a link or a stop builds, exactly as before, and redraws both panels with them. A panel is cleared and rebuilt only when its overlay switched or the link names its tool anew; otherwise it is redrawn into what is there, as a reader's own edit is. `replaced` now fires only on a rebuild.
- The overlay panel is drawn once at startup, after the story column exists, because None's starting points list the stories. That used to happen as a side effect of every link and stop.
- The tools plan is marked done, with step 3 (typing overlay ids and settings per text) dropped.

A first version kept the held settings whenever a link wrote the same ones. Review showed that keeps what a link does not carry: a Haftarah story stop's `reading`, a hover preview, and colours a new search could then share with an overlay. So the tools are always rebuilt, and only the panel's redraw changes.

**Checks.**
- Unit tests: 3,206 passed, including one for `linked`.
- A new layout test pins a verse, unpins it with Escape, presses Back, and checks both panels' controls are the same elements as before. It fails without the change.
- Layout suite: 510 passed. Loading suite: 51 passed, run by hand.

**To look at on the preview:** search for a word, open the search panel, pin a verse, press Escape, then Back. The panel should stay put rather than flash or scroll back to the top. Story scrolling, especially through the Haftarah story, should look the same as before.

nodes.title: VIS: a paper with no text lights in full, a little dimmer
nodes.body:
A friend looked up Jeffrey Heer under **Authors**. The card says 4 papers, but only three showed, and one of those lit a single square.

The other two are papers with no full text: the VISxAI interactive article (Mon 13:00) and "Crossing the Chasm" (Thu 13:24, in *From design spaces to visual design*). Their squares stand in for text we don't have, and each carries a thin grey ring. A ring is a fixed number of screen pixels wide, so on a small square it covers the whole square and hides the colour the overlay gives it. Crossing the Chasm showed only its abstract square, which has no ring; the VISxAI article showed nothing.

Two changes:

- A square an overlay makes stand out gets no ring (`fillDefaultColors`, `packages/shell/src/itemColoring.ts`). Unlit squares keep their rings.
- So a lit paper with no text still reads as missing, its stand-in squares keep 60% of the pick's colour (`PLACEHOLDER_KEEPS`, `apps/ieeevis/src/overlays/listOverlay.ts`). A real abstract stays full strength. This holds for authors, keywords and the two citation overlays, which share that code.

**Before:** in the right-hand column, *From design spaces to visual design* lights one square.
![heer-before](https://github.com/danyelf/torahmap/blob/399648119b14bbb57eb1c9754090bf27419b9e50/heer-before.png?raw=true)

**After:** all four papers light. The two with no text, Monday's at the bottom left and Thursday's, are dimmer than the two on Tuesday.
![heer-dimmed](https://github.com/danyelf/torahmap/blob/399648119b14bbb57eb1c9754090bf27419b9e50/heer-dimmed.png?raw=true)

The strengths compared, 45% on top, 60% (chosen) in the middle and 75% at the bottom. Left is Monday's paper with no text, middle is a Tuesday paper with full text, and right is Crossing the Chasm, whose abstract square stays bright.
![dim-compare](https://github.com/danyelf/torahmap/blob/399648119b14bbb57eb1c9754090bf27419b9e50/dim-compare.png?raw=true)

**To look:** on the preview, open the VIS map with `?overlay=authors&authors=Jeffrey Heer`.

Closes #575

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Reviewed up to `0c99799b`

🤖 Claude: a fresh reviewer that hadn't seen the discussion read it for correctness and for duplication. It found nothing to fix.

- **Every caller and every overlay that lights squares (Talmud hadran ring, VIS stand-in squares, search, the cross-fade):** correct. In a cross-fade a square counts as lit if either side lights it, so no ring flickers. Kept as is.
- **The comment "a small square is all ring" might be unmeasured:** it holds. The ring is a fixed width in screen pixels (`u_ring.x / u_zoom`, `webgl.ts:96`), and a square smaller on screen than `u_ring.z` has no hole, so it is drawn entirely in the ring colour (`webgl.ts:121`). Kept.

nodes.title: Code map: a SeeSoft-style map of a pull request
nodes.body:
A map of this repo in the manner of SeeSoft: every line of code is a bar in a fixed place, shaped by its indent and length. It is coloured by what this pull request did to each line, by churn, by line type, or by file type. Every folder is a box, at every depth, and every file sits on a faint shade with its name above it. It answers "1,200 lines changed in 53 files — *which* 53?" at a glance. Preview only: the live site does not build it.

**Look at it:** https://codemap-design-torahmap.danyel.workers.dev/codemap/

- **☰ → Overlay → Pull request.** Green is added, amber changed, red where lines were removed. `apps/codemap` and `scripts/codemap` should be all green. The ‹ › buttons step through the commits one at a time.
- **Churn:** when each line last changed, or how many times, over the whole history.
- **Line type:** blank, comment, import, function or class opening, code.
- **File type:** code, prose, scripts, styles and pages, data and settings, by the file’s ending.
- **Folders and files.** Folder names keep their size on screen: outer folders first, deeper ones as you zoom in. File names show once you zoom in far enough for them to fit above their file. A file wraps into a new column every 200 lines.
- **Pan and zoom.** At about 139,000 lines this is the biggest map the engine has drawn, more than the Talmud's 81,793 squares. Smoothness has not been measured: headless browsers draw without the graphics card.

**Making the data for a pull request:** `npm run codemap` on its branch writes `public/data/codemap/` (see "Code map data" in `docs/working-in-the-repo.md`). It takes about a minute for this repo. Two open PRs that both carry the data conflict; run it again to settle the conflict.

Design: `docs/plans/2026-11-02-code-map-design.md`.

### Pictures

![codemap-default--desktop](https://github.com/danyelf/torahmap/blob/c00bf64d9754a780368cb646f4553f721ad07349/codemap-default--desktop.png?raw=true)
![codemap-default--phone](https://github.com/danyelf/torahmap/blob/c00bf64d9754a780368cb646f4553f721ad07349/codemap-default--phone.png?raw=true)
![codemap-file--desktop](https://github.com/danyelf/torahmap/blob/c00bf64d9754a780368cb646f4553f721ad07349/codemap-file--desktop.png?raw=true)
![codemap-file--phone](https://github.com/danyelf/torahmap/blob/c00bf64d9754a780368cb646f4553f721ad07349/codemap-file--phone.png?raw=true)
![codemap-kind--desktop](https://github.com/danyelf/torahmap/blob/c00bf64d9754a780368cb646f4553f721ad07349/codemap-kind--desktop.png?raw=true)
![codemap-kind--phone](https://github.com/danyelf/torahmap/blob/c00bf64d9754a780368cb646f4553f721ad07349/codemap-kind--phone.png?raw=true)
![codemap-pr--desktop](https://github.com/danyelf/torahmap/blob/c00bf64d9754a780368cb646f4553f721ad07349/codemap-pr--desktop.png?raw=true)
![codemap-pr--phone](https://github.com/danyelf/torahmap/blob/c00bf64d9754a780368cb646f4553f721ad07349/codemap-pr--phone.png?raw=true)

### Open questions for Danyel

- **The opening view fits the whole repo.** A link with an overlay but no camera opens at a fixed zoom (0.05), which fits the repo’s height on a desktop; the shell gives such links a fixed zoom, not the fitted one.
- **Folder boxes are drawn over the bars,** as the VIS map’s panels are, so their tints add up: a bar in a folder three deep is lightened about a fifth of the way toward the tint. The mockup drew them under the bars. Putting them under needs a layer of the shell’s beneath the canvas, or a blend; say if the dulling shows.
- **Moiré:** none at screen density 2. At 1.5 there is mild uneven striping inside dense columns, most visible at zoom 0.22, with no bands across the map. Checked at rest only, and before the folder boxes; not checked again since.
- **What is drawn:** `docs/` is the largest folder (about 41,600 lines). `data/`, downloaded files and two generated AI Act JSON files are left out.
- **Churn and formatting commits:** "when last changed" skips the formatting commits listed in `.git-blame-ignore-revs` (git blame honours it); "how many times" counts them.
- **One shared change:** on touch screens, segmented buttons are at least 24px wide (`packages/shell/src/styles/controls.css`), for the ‹ › buttons. Every map's layout tests pass.

Closes #563
